analysis.title: Everyone Is Dumping AI... And The Anti-AI Trade Is Exploding
key_insights: Tech credit spreads are widening alongside falling tech stocks, so credit and equities now agree. The prior CDS spike was met with a surging NDX.
VXN is approaching its September highs, but volatility has been range-bound for two months.

Global systematic L/S fell 1.4% in one day, a nearly four-standard-deviation move. The pain is in gross exposure, with violent short squeezes alongside heavy selling in longs, which points to de-grossing.
Privorotsky expects more choppiness but is increasingly optimistic that semis have priced in much of the bad news. A possible relative-value trade is short hyperscalers versus semis.
Systematic multi-strat funds had a 2.2 sigma negative performance day but are still up 20% YTD.

Goldman data shows foreign investors sold $11.6B of Korean tech over eight consecutive sessions. SK Hynix has had 15 straight days of foreign selling and Samsung five. Domestic institutions and retail are absorbing some of the supply.

Goldman reports hedge funds have been net sellers of global AI stocks for five consecutive sessions. Net allocation fell to 26.1% from a June peak of 31.7%. The aggregate long/short ratio fell from 4.34 to 3.27, in the seventh percentile over the past year.
NDX forward P/E is back near 21x, revisiting the lows seen since the AI cycle began in 2023. Peter Callahan says this could support heading into earnings season.

DDR5 spot prices keep rising while memory equities have been hit. Goldman notes Samsung trades near 1.2x book and SK Hynix near 0.9x, consistent with investors discounting a significant downturn by 2028.
NIFTY and KOSPI have moved in a nearly inverse relationship this year. India's software services sector is up 7.5% this week, helped by optimism after Accenture's investor day.
MSCI India outperformed MSCI Asia Pacific ex-Japan by 9.7 percentage points this week, the biggest weekly relative move since May 2009.
EWZ implied volatility (VXEWZ) is at its highest since the Covid shock ahead of the Brazilian election, while the ETF itself has barely moved.

sector_views.rationale: Privorotsky sees semis at levels where much of the bad news is priced in, while expecting more choppiness.
Software services rose 7.5% this week as regional allocators rotated out of AI-linked Asian tech.

earnings_insights: NDX forward P/E near 21x could give a supportive backdrop into earnings season, with earnings potentially doing some of the heavy lifting (Peter Callahan).

trade_ideas.rationale: Privorotsky thinks semis have priced in much of the bad news after the selloff.

risk_factors: Further de-grossing and choppiness in long/short strategies.
Continued foreign selling of Korean tech, with limited capacity for domestic buyers to absorb it.

tension_points.bull_case: Valuations are back near AI-cycle lows (NDX forward P/E about 21x), bullish positioning has been flushed out, and DDR5 spot prices are still rising, so the memory equity selloff may be ahead of fundamentals.
tension_points.bear_case: Credit spreads are widening with falling tech stocks, hedge funds are de-grossing, and foreign investors continue heavy selling of Korean tech.

theme_stances.key_argument: Much of the bullish AI positioning has been flushed out and valuations are near cycle lows.
